title: Study on Modified Effects of Localized Radiotherapy on Kids’ Olfactory Sensation
summary:
The aim of the study is to investigate radiation therapy-induced changes in olfactory perception in pediatric patients and their correlation with intracerebral tumors and tumors located in head, neck and ears. Therefore, olfactory function will be assessed at specific time points (before radiation therapy, at the end of radiation therapy, and 3 and 12 months after completion of radiation therapy) as follows:

• Conducting olfactory tests using the Sniffin’ Sticks-USNIFF test to assess odor identification. The test consists of 12 felt-tip pens filled with scents. 
• Measuring the odor threshold to assess the sensitivity of the sense of smell and the function of the olfactory mucosa.
• Subjective aspects of the sense of smell are assessed using age-appropriate questionnaires, including an evaluation of perceived olfactory ability using a visual analog scale (VAS) and the use of the validated SoSAL questionnaire to assess olfactory impairments in children.

Particular attention is paid to the influence of radiation therapy on the age-dependent development of the sense of smell. The identification of potential risk factors and recovery mechanisms is intended to contribute to improving the long-term quality of life for pediatric cancer survivors.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients aged ≥ 4 and ≤ 17 years
• Patients who are indicated for curative radio(chemo)therapy in one of the target volumes listed above
• Written consent from the legal guardian(s); if the patient is capable of giving informed consent, consent from the patient is also required
Exclusion criteria:
• Metastatic tumors for which curative radiation therapy is not indicated
• Patients who are unable to attend follow-up appointments (due to limiting barriers, such as language barriers or severe neurological impairments)
• Patients with contraindications for MRI examinations (e.g., pacemakers, defibrillators, neurostimulators, aneurysm clips, cochlear implants, permanent makeup, metal fragments, or, in some cases, osteosynthetic implants)
• Lack of motivation or resilience on the part of the patients
• Lack of language skills to complete the study procedures
